To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the concentrations of Ca, Cu, Mg and Zn in the arterial wall were different in atherosclerosis obliteration and abdominal aorticaneurysm and that the concentrations of these elements in plaque were higher than in the surrounding aortic wall.

the concentrations of calcium, magnesium zinc and copper are higher in atherosclerosis and lower in aneurysm, that the ratios of calcium/magnesium, calcium/zinc and magnesium/copper are higher in aneurysms than in atherosclerosis, that positive correlations are found between the concentrations of calcium/magnesum, calcium/zinc, and magnesium/zinc in the arterial wall of both atherosclerosis and aneurysms, and that copper concentrations in serum correlate with copper concentrations
the concentrations of Ca, Cu, Mg and Zn were higher in plaque and lower in the arterial wall as compared to the surrounding tissue.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship of the concentrations of Ca, Cu and Zn in the arterial wall with the serum and the calcified plaque in AO and AA.
the role of the trace element concentrations and their ratios in the pathogenesis of AO and AA.
the changes in the arterial wall composition in atherosclerosis and aneurysms.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the differences in the concentrations of these elements in AO and AA are not only due to the presence of the plaque but also to the changes in serum concentrations of these elements and the changes in the arterial wall.
the concentrations of Ca, Zn and Mg in the arterial wall were higher and those of Cu lower in AO than in AA.
the differences in concentrations of Ca, Zn and Cu in AO and AA and their accumulation in the plaque are of importance in the pathophysiological mechanisms of these diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in AO, the serum concentrations of Ca are lower and those of Zn and Cu are higher than in AA.

the changes of serum concentrations and the arterial concentrations of Ca, Cu, Zn, and Mg in the arterial wall of patients with atherosclerotic occlusive disease (AO) are different from those with abdominal aortic aneuysm (AA), and the accumulation of the mentioned elements in the plaque is more pronounced.
atherosclerosis is a multifactorial disease and that the role of trace elements in this disease is not fully understood.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is a relationship between the serum and the arterial concentrations of these elements in AO and AA, but this relationship is different between AO and AA.
the accumulation of these metals in the aortic wall and plaque formation may play a role in atherosclerosis.
